title: move X --before X drops the item from the in-memory index
findings_note: severity revised: cosmetic since the error envelope landed

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`ops.move` pops the item out of the list before computing its target index. When the
target is the item itself, `index.position(X)` is then asked about a list that no longer
contains it.

**Severity revised (2026-09-24).** As filed, this dropped the item from the in-memory
index: `position` raised a bare `KeyError`, the item was never reinserted and
`save_index` was never reached. The error-envelope work made `position` raise
`StateError(code="no_such_item")` instead, which the CLI now reports cleanly and exits 2.
Disk was never touched either way, so what remains is a confusing message — `no such
item: S01` about an item that plainly exists — rather than data loss.

Still worth fixing, but it is a wording bug now, not a corruption one.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `Move_BeforeItself_IsANoOpAndKeepsTheItem` — assert the item is still present and the
   position is unchanged.
2. `Move_AfterItself_IsANoOp`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Resolve the target position before popping, or short-circuit when the target id equals
the moving id. The second is clearer and says what it means.

**Not in this slice:** moving several items at once.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Full suite, plus the TUI reorder keys.
